h: Preparing Every Soul for the Resting of the Shechinah

p: Now, to understand the order of the parshiyos
קוֹדֶם פָּרָשַׁת וַיְהִי בְּיוֹם כַּלֹּת מֹשֶׁה
before the parsha of "And it was on the day that Moshe finished":
where the counting of the hosts of the Torah
and the hosts of the Mishkan is mentioned
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב זֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ רֵישׁ חֵלֶק ג)
(as written in the holy Zohar at the beginning of volume III, Zohar III 117b),
and after the counting of the Levi'im was completed,
who guard the charge of the Mishkan of Testimony,
הָיָה רָאוּי לִכְתּוֹב אַחַר כָּךְ תֵּיכֶף
it would have been fitting to write immediately afterward
the parsha "And it was on the day that Moshe finished,"
for then the completeness of the union was finished,
of Kudsha Brich Hu and His Shechinah,
on the day that the bride entered the chuppah.
And although the parsha of sending out the impure
also has a connection to this,
for it is to purify the camp
so that there be completeness of the union,
but what does the theft from a convert have to do
after the asham for theft was already mentioned
and the Ra'aya Mehemna on this parsha
as the root of the mitzvah of teshuvah.
And also, what do the parsha of the sotah
and the parsha of the nazir have to do here,
קוֹדֶם לְפָרָשַׁת וַיְהִי בְּיוֹם כַּלֹּת מֹשֶׁה
before the parsha "And it was on the day that Moshe finished"?
that this is precisely the preparation
for there to be completed through this
the completeness of the union for the souls of Yisrael,
יֵשׁ לוֹ שַׁיָּיכוּת לִקְדוּשַּׁת כְּנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל
has a connection to the holiness of Knesses Yisrael,
so that through it too there be completed
"And they shall send out of the camp
and everyone impure through a dead body" (Bamidbar 5:2);
these allude to the three blemishes
Tzarua alludes to jealousy and anger
(as they expounded on "This is the law of the metzora":
motzi ra, one who brings out evil) (Arachin 15b),
and impurity through a dead body
comes on account of honor and self-elevation,
עַל יְדֵי הַסָּתַת הַנָּחָשׁ בַּחֵטְא הָרִאשׁוֹן
through the incitement of the serpent in the first sin,
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה נִקְנְסָה עֲלֵיהֶם מִיתָה
and through this death was decreed upon them,
in the words "For you are dust,
and to dust you shall return" (Bereishis 3:19),
so that he has nothing in which to elevate himself.
וּכְדֵי שֶׁלֹּא יִפּוֹל לֵב הָאָדָם עָלָיו
And so that a person's heart should not fall within him,
כָּל אֶחָד כְּפִי מַה שֶּׁיּוֹדֵעַ נִגְעֵי לְבָבוֹ
each one according to what he knows of the afflictions of his heart,
שֶׁאֵינֶנּוּ נָקִי מִג׳ פְּגָמִים הַנִּזְכָּרִים לְעֵיל
that he is not clean of the three blemishes mentioned above,
from the holiness of Knesses Yisrael,
as it says, "And they shall send out" etc.,
the parsha of theft from a convert,
to teach that for everything there is a repair,
even what seems to a person's grasp
כְּעִנְיַן גֶּזֶל הַגֵּר שֶׁאֵין לוֹ יוֹרְשִׁים
like theft from a convert who has no heirs,
where teshuvah would not help him,
וְהוּא מִן הָעֲבֵירוֹת שֶׁבֵּין אָדָם לַחֲבֵירוֹ
and it is one of the sins between man and his fellow,
which is not atoned through teshuvah
וְעִם כָּל זֶה נָתְנָה לוֹ הַתּוֹרָה עֵצָה
And nevertheless the Torah gave him counsel,
that for this too there is a repair:
that he give the restitution through the Kohen.
the allusion to the root of the mitzvah of teshuvah
it is possible for there to be repaired

p: וְאַחַר זֶה בָּא פָּרָשַׁת סוֹטָה גַּם כֵּן
After this comes the parsha of the sotah, also
to teach that Hashem Yisbarach devises means
לְבִלְתִּי יִדַּח מִמֶּנּוּ נִדָּח (שְׁמוּאֵל ב יד, יד)
"that the banished one not be banished from Him" (Shmuel II 14:14),
that even from the utmost distance
there is hope for a Jewish soul
to return to the root of the holiness of Knesses Yisrael.
And this is what is mentioned in the oath of the curse:
יִתֵּן ה׳ אוֹתָךְ לְאָלָה וְגוֹ׳ (בְּמִדְבַּר ה, כא)
"May Hashem make you a curse" etc. (Bamidbar 5:21).
And it is truly a great wonder
that there is mentioned in this
the Name Havayah, blessed be He;
that HaKadosh Baruch Hu does not
not even the name Elohim is said,
רַק סְתָם וְלַחֹשֶׁךְ קָרָא לָיְלָה (בְּרֵאשִׁית א, ה)
only, without a name, "and the darkness He called night" (Bereishis 1:5)
even though the darkness is for the sake of the light,
that it be recognized through it.
And all the more so here,
שֶׁנִּזְכַּר עוֹד הַשֵּׁם הֲוָיָ״ה בָּרוּךְ הוּא
where moreover the Name Havayah, blessed be He, is mentioned,
and it is also mentioned in the language of giving:
and as is known, this is the language of a gift,
as our Sages, of blessed memory, said
עַל ג׳ דְּבָרִים שֶׁנִּיתְּנוּ מַתָּנָה לָעוֹלָם
about three things that were given as a gift to the world,
because the language of giving is said of them
However, it is as mentioned above,
that in truth it is a good and great gift
as we said on this matter
regarding the rebukes in Mishneh Torah,
which are also said in this language:
יִתֵּן ה׳ אֶת מְטַר אַרְצְךָ וְגוֹ׳ (דְּבָרִים כח, כד)
"Hashem will make the rain of your land" etc. (Devarim 28:24);
וְגַם בְּכוּלָּם נִזְכַּר שֵׁם הֲוָיָ״ה בָּרוּךְ הוּא
and in all of them, too, the Name Havayah, blessed be He, is mentioned.
And this is only to teach
שֶׁכָּל הַתּוֹכָחוֹת הֵמָּה בְּחִינַת רַחֲמִים גְּדוֹלִים
that all the rebukes are an aspect of great mercy,
כַּאֲשֶׁר יְיַסֵּר אִישׁ אֶת בְּנוֹ (דְּבָרִים ח, ה)
וְאֶת אֲשֶׁר יֶאֱהַב ה׳ יוֹכִיחַ (מִשְׁלֵי ג, יב)
in order to bring him back to the root of holiness.
And likewise here with the sotah,
where there is no utmost distance greater than this:
שֶׁגַּם לְאַחַר שֶׁנִּמְחַק הַשֵּׁם הֲוָיָ״ה עַל הַמַּיִם
for even after the Name Havayah was erased upon the water,
which was only in order to make peace
between a man and his wife,
so that if she was defiled she would confess,
and this one stands in her rebellion,
to fear the punishment of the water,
and this is casting off the yoke,
to deny the Providence from Above
in the utmost concealment, chas veshalom;
עִם כָּל זֶה בָּא לָהּ מַתָּנָה טוֹבָה
nevertheless a good gift comes to her
to bring her back to the root of holiness,
עַל יְדֵי שֶׁיִּקּוּיַּים בָּהּ תֵּיכֶף הָעוֹנֶשׁ
through the punishment being fulfilled in her immediately;
and then she will feel in her soul
then her uncircumcised heart will be humbled,
and through this she will have a repair,
to bring her back to the root of holiness.

p: After this the parsha of the nazir is mentioned,
that there is counsel to be guarded beforehand,
לְבַל יִהְיֶה נִפְתֶּה לְג׳ פְּגָמִים הַנִּזְכָּרִים לְעֵיל
so as not to be enticed into the three blemishes mentioned above,
from which the nazir must separate himself.
is the repair of jealousy and anger,
as is known that hairs indicate judgment,
כִּי עֵשָׂו אִישׁ שָׂעִיר (בְּרֵאשִׁית כז, יא)
as our Sages, of blessed memory, said:
And the impurity of a corpse
is from the blemish of honor, as mentioned above.
וְהַיְינוּ עַל יְדֵי שֶׁיִּהְיֶה לוֹ אִתְעָרוּתָא
That is, through his having an awakening
to sanctify himself in what is permitted to him,
כִּי עַל זֶה נִקְרָא חוֹטֵא (נָזִיר יט, א)
for on account of this he is called a sinner (Nazir 19a),
כִּי דַּיֶּיךָ מַה שֶּׁאָסְרָה תּוֹרָה (יְרוּשַׁלְמִי נְדָרִים ט, א)
for "enough for you what the Torah forbade" (Yerushalmi Nedarim 9:1);
רַק כְּעִנְיַן נָזִיר שֶׁל שִׁמְעוֹן הַצַּדִּיק
rather, like the matter of the nazir of Shimon HaTzaddik
וְעַל יְדֵי שֶׁעוֹשֶׂה בְּתוֹרַת גָּדֵר לְעַצְמוֹ
and by his doing it as a fence for himself,
in order to be guarded from the yetzer hara,
even if he afflicts himself a little,
through this he is called holy;
and as in the words of the Ramban, of blessed memory,
עַל פָּסוּק קְדוֹשִׁים תִּהְיוּ (וַיִּקְרָא יט, ב)
on the pasuk "You shall be holy" (Vayikra 19:2),
who counted this as a positive mitzvah:
to sanctify oneself in what is permitted to him,
כָּל אֶחָד לְפִי מַה שֶּׁמַּרְגִּישׁ בְּנַפְשׁוֹ
each according to what he feels in his soul
of the afflictions of his heart,
so as not to be a degenerate with the Torah's license.
After this Birkas Kohanim is stated,
וּפֵירֵשׁ בְּבַמִּדְבַּר רַבָּה רֵישׁ פָּרָשָׁה יא
and Bamidbar Rabbah at the beginning of chapter 11 explains (Bamidbar Rabbah 11:1)
that it is juxtaposed to say
שֶׁאִם נָזְרוּ וְכוּלֵּי לְהִשָּׁמֵר מִן הָעֲבֵירָה
that if they abstained, etc., to guard themselves from sin,
that whoever separates himself for the sake of Heaven
And this is "for the sake of Heaven":
in order to be guarded from sin,
that one must fence himself in what is permitted
so that he not come to what is forbidden.
And about this they said in Nazir (Nazir 4b):
"May there be many like you who take the vow of nezirus," etc.
וְשָׁם בְּבַמִּדְבַּר רַבָּה רֵישׁ פָּרָשָׁה יב
And there, in Bamidbar Rabbah at the beginning of chapter 12 (Bamidbar Rabbah 12:2):
I come laden with blessings," etc.
בְּרֶמֶז אָמַר לָהֶם הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא
By allusion HaKadosh Baruch Hu told them
that they should make the Mishkan,
for He gives them blessings with His coming,
אָבוֹא אֵלֶיךָ וּבֵרַכְתִּיךָ כּוּלֵּי (שְׁמוֹת כ, כא)
"I will come to you and bless you" etc. (Shemos 20:21);
therefore it says "May He bless you" etc.,
Now in the pasuk of "I will come"
He put the coming before the blessings,
and here He put the blessing
before "on the day that... finished," which is the coming.
And the reason is that they are in truth
at one and the same time,
and therefore sometimes this is put first
in the manner of what they said about Moshe and Aharon,
לוֹמַר שֶׁשְּׁנֵיהֶם שְׁקוּלִים (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה א, טו)
to say that both are equal (Bereishis Rabbah 1:15);
and likewise further in the Mishnah at the end of Kerisus.
וְעַל כֵּן אָמַר אַחַר פָּרָשַׁת נָזִיר
And therefore after the parsha of the nazir it said
Birkas Kohanim and "on the day that... finished,"
דְּזוֹכֶה עַל יְדֵי זֶה לְהַשְׁרָאַת הַשְּׁכִינָה
for through this one merits the resting of the Shechinah,
וְאֵין הַבְּרָכָה אֶלָּא עַל יְדֵי זֶה
and the blessing is only through this.
For in the three blessings of Birkas Kohanim
the Name Havayah is mentioned in each one,
for He is the One Who blesses;
וְסִיֵּים וְשָׂמוּ אֶת שְׁמִי וְגוֹ׳ (בְּמִדְבַּר ו, כז)
and it concluded, "And they shall place My Name" etc. (Bamidbar 6:27).
The meaning of "and they shall place"
כְּמוֹ אֲשֶׁר תָּשִׂים לִפְנֵיהֶם (שְׁמוֹת כא, א)
is like "which you shall set before them" (Shemos 21:1)
at the beginning of Parshas Mishpatim,
which Targum Onkelos renders "which you shall arrange";
and in Rashi there, from the Mechilta:
that he should explain to them the reason of the matter.
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמַרְנוּ עַל אַתָּה אֶחָד וְשִׁמְךָ אֶחָד
as we said about "You are One and Your Name is One":
which is not pronounced in this world,
וְשִׁמְךָ הוּא שֵׁם אֲדֹנָ״י שֶׁבּוֹ נִקְרָא
and "Your Name" is the Name Adnus, by which He is called;
for the name by which He is called
is what is grasped in a person's heart,
for this Name indicates the Shechinah,
in the hearts of Bnei Yisrael.
at the beginning of the passage beginning "And they shall place":
"they shall arrange, as it is said,
the crowns of the right to the right," etc.;
and as will be explained below.)
"and I will bless them," as mentioned above.
And this too is the matter of
"He blessed and He sanctified" of the day of Shabbos,
that everything is in world, year and soul,
is like the Mikdash in the world
and the Kohen in the soul.
as written at the beginning of Parshas Emor
several times, and in Parshas Korach.)
For on the day of Shabbos
is the revelation of His holiness in the world,
that is, the revelation of the Shechinah,
עַל פָּסוּק הַשַּׁבָּת לְדֹרֹתָם (שְׁמוֹת לא, טז)
on the pasuk "the Shabbos for their generations" (Shemos 31:16):
in the two chambers of the heart";
and did not explain the nature of the blessing,
as it explained in the blessing of man and of the fish.
הוּא עַל יְדֵי בִּיאָתוֹ לִשְׁכּוֹן בֵּינֵיהֶם
is through His coming to dwell among them,
that they merited the blessing of HaKadosh Baruch Hu
(and Shabbos is called a bride in perek Kol Kisvei (Shabbos 119a)
and at the end of chapter 10 of Bereishis Rabbah (Bereishis Rabbah 10:9);
as written in the Midrash (Bamidbar Rabbah 12:8)
on the pasuk "on the day that Moshe finished");
and in the Ra'aya Mehemna, Pinchas (Zohar III 245a):
"and they are 'May Hashem bless you'" etc.;
that the twelve loaves of the showbread
of the three Names Havayah of Birkas Kohanim
(and likewise there are twelve words there
and this is as we said,
that the blessing of Shabbos is Birkas Kohanim.
And the main blessing is in eating,
"He blessed it with the manna" (Bereishis Rabbah 11:2),
And after all these it says,
וַיְהִי בְּיוֹם כַּלֹּת מֹשֶׁה (בְּמִדְבַּר ז, א)
"And it was on the day that Moshe finished" (Bamidbar 7:1),
שֶׁעַל יְדֵי זֶה נִגְמַר שְׁלֵימוּת הַיִּחוּד
for through this the completeness of the union was finished,
of Kudsha Brich Hu and His Shechinah,
עַל יְדֵי כָּל פְּרָטֵי נַפְשׁוֹת יִשְׂרָאֵל
through all the individual souls of Yisrael;
they were all repaired for the good,

rich.text: “ויהי ביום כלות משה להקים את המשכן וימשח אתו ויקדש אתו ואת כל כליו ואת המזבח ואת כל כליו וימשחם ויקדש אתם”

paragraphs.text: Source: Tehillim 125:5 — “והמטים עקלקלותם יוליכם יהוה את פעלי האון שלום על ישראל” — “But those who in their crookedness act corruptly, let GOD make them go the way of evildoers. May it be well with Israel!”

rich.text: “והמטים עקלקלותם יוליכם יהוה את פעלי האון שלום על ישראל”
